First Degree Burns

First degree burn

Injury localized to the epidermis

Presentation

Reddened skin means that the dermis is intact

Skin is dry

Pain at burn site means that the nerve endings in the reticular dermis are intact

Burned skin is blanch to touch meaning when press with your finger against the burned skin it turns to white color and then when release finger it is back to red color meaning the blood vessels in the dermis are intact

First degree burns are NOT associated with blisters

Healing

First degree burns heals perfectly without scarring

Examples: sun burn, minor scald from kitchen accident

Treatment is to relieve pain with topical soothing agents like cool water for 10- 20 min, aloe vera gel, silver sulfadiazine cream, Vaseline +/- NSAIDs

First degree burns heals in 4 days to a week

Repeated sunburns increase the risk of skin cancer
